question: Which of the following is the correct sequence of alkaline earth metals, according to atomic number?
solution:
The correct answer is **Be [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alkaline earth metals** are elements in Group 2 of the periodic table.
 
• The elements in this group include **beryllium (Be), magnesium (Mg), calcium (Ca), strontium (Sr), and barium (Ba)**.
 
• The correct sequence of these elements by atomic number is **Be

• **Alkaline earth metals** have two electrons in their outermost shell.
 
• They are known for their **reactivity**, which increases as you move down the group.
 
• These metals are typically **shiny, silvery-white**, and are good conductors of electricity.
 
• They form **basic oxides** and hydroxides.
 
• Common uses include **magnesium in aircraft construction** and **calcium in cement and bones**.
